metadata.title: Madison, Week Two
notes: DESIGN-STAGE progress update. HONESTY IS THE CONSTRAINT: nothing is built, so no beat shows tool output. B06's scored output is tabbed 'design target, not produced' and closes with '// NOT OUTPUT.'; B07's figure carries 'illustrative - not a produced result'; B10 states status including 'nothing built' and 'no sample data yet'; BVDT closes on the same. B01's correction (built -> designed) puts the honesty on screen first.
Collaborator and tool names are kept GENERIC by request: 'the section-five methodology' and 'design review', with no personal names and no internal tool names on screen or in voice.
folderLabel is a PER-BEAT prop on every ClaudeComposerAsk beat (B00, B05, BHTF). metadata.folderLabel alone is NOT read by the component - its schema defaults to '@NikBearBrown'.
B01 triggerWords is a SINGLE TOKEN ('built'), occurring once. buildActs() matches triggers per whitespace-delimited token; a multi-word trigger silently never fires. The replacement may be a phrase.
B01 typing is paced in absolute ms (charMs), not as a fraction of the beat, so it is tuned to FIT the measured window. Verify the FINAL frame, not just the gate.
Every beat carries durationInSeconds so its composition re-times via calculateMetadata instead of truncating.
BVDT artifactLines contain NO empty strings: ClaudeVerdictArtifact numbers every line and does not filter blanks.
ChipGrid beats (B08, B10) run cols=3 with 5-6 items = two rows, so the caption slot does not collide (unlike a 12-chip four-row grid).
REUSE ONLY - no new components were built for this reel.

Compiled WITHOUT --review as requested, which takes the master path and runs final_frame_check.py (GATE V) as a hard gate. If it refuses, the refusal is reported rather than silently switching to the review path.

beats.narration_text: Hi, my name is Prashanth, and this video is a progress update on the Madison brand-archetype detector. Last time I had a scope. This week I have a technical design, and one thing I am blocked on. Nothing is built yet, and I will be specific about that.

shot.new_visual_element: the composer answering what moved this week, with the status stated plainly
shot.visual_intent: COLD OPEN LAW - opens on the Claude UI and the ask lands answered. The output lines are a status report, NOT detector output: nothing is built, so showing a result would be fabrication

the question types itself into the composer as the voice finishes the introduction
send button arms terracotta - the one accent in the frame
running indicator reads 'reading this week's notes...'
three output lines land: what moved, what is blocked, and the status - design started, not built

props.command: What moved on Madison this week?
output: → this week      a technical design for the Ruler archetype
→ blocked on     sample data — format, count, owner
→ status         design started — NOT built, no results

beats.narration_text: This week I designed the detector. One archetype first, Ruler, the luxury one. Inputs, scoring, evaluation. Design, not code. That distinction is the whole point of this update, so I will keep it honest.

shot.new_visual_element: the overview written, reconsidered, and corrected on screen
shot.visual_intent: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW - the whole idea in one breath. The correction is the misconception a progress update invites: that 'progress' means something got built. Striking 'built' for 'designed' makes the honesty the first thing on screen

show.event: 0.8s of silence - the caret blinks on an empty cream page before the voice starts
writer types 'This week I built the detector.' - 'built' turns terracotta, marked for deletion
a full beat of hesitation, then 'built' deletes
'designed' types in its place
the two remaining lines type in: 'One archetype first: Ruler.' / 'Inputs, scoring, evaluation.'
corrected sentence holds on screen through the cut

props.text:
This week I built the detector.
One archetype first: Ruler.
Inputs, scoring, evaluation.

beats.narration_text: Here is the problem in one question. A luxury brand can be unmistakably Ruler and never once use the word luxury. Its copy says heritage, mastery, by appointment. So could you detect the archetype by searching for keywords? Commit to yes or no.

shot.new_visual_element: predict card - the viewer commits before the reveal
shot.visual_intent: Plain move 2 and move 4 together - builds the plausible wrong guess (keyword matching) and plants the ONE running example, the luxury brand that never says 'luxury', to be paid off at B07

show.event: question card fades up on the cream stage
the three real copy phrases sit under it, ink on cream - heritage, mastery, by appointment
commit line appears in terracotta - the one accent - asking for an answer now
card holds still, giving the viewer real time to choose

props.question: A brand reads unmistakably Ruler but never says “luxury.” Could keyword matching detect it?
props.commit: commit to yes or no before the next beat

beats.narration_text: So this week I took the section-five methodology and turned it into a concrete design, in three parts. Inputs: what text goes in, and in what format. Scoring: how we measure that text against the Ruler trait profile. Evaluation: how we prove the score is right. Those three are the whole design.

shot.new_visual_element: the three parts of the technical design as a stack
shot.visual_intent: FRAMEWORK beat - all three parts presented BEFORE any of them is explained, and left as the reel's reference figure. Evaluation is accented because it is the part that makes the other two trustworthy

show.event: part one stacks in: inputs - what text goes in, and in what format
part two stacks beneath it: scoring - measured against the Ruler trait profile
part three stacks in terracotta: evaluation - how we prove the score is right
caption settles - a methodology turned into something buildable

beats.narration_text: Inputs first. The detector reads what a brand actually publishes: website copy, social captions, the tagline, and probably a competitor or two for contrast. Not a questionnaire, and not adjectives the brand chose for itself. One flag: how much archetype signal that published copy really carries is exactly what evaluation has to settle.

shot.new_visual_element: the brand's published text flowing into the detector
shot.visual_intent: Plain move 3 - the mechanism once, plainly, with EXACTLY ONE inference flag placed on whether published copy carries archetype signal at all. That is the project's genuine unknown and it is why evaluation exists

show.event: dark rack labelled 'what the brand publishes' builds on the left
four source chips fly along the arc into the detector: website copy, social captions, the tagline, competitor copy
the window's task line reads 'is this brand a Ruler?'
the first chip checks off in terracotta as it lands; the others stay ink
settle line reads: published text, never self-reported adjectives

props.arcCaption: real published copy — not a questionnaire

beats.narration_text: Scoring is the part that has to be defensible. Here is the shape I am designing toward.

shot.visual_intent: ASK->RESULT LAW - the scoring figure at B06 is preceded by the actual prompt that produces it, so the pair reads as a receipt

props.command: Sketch the scored output for one brand against the Ruler trait profile. Every score must carry the line of copy it came from.

beats.narration_text: Every trait gets a score, and every score carries the line of copy it came from. Ruler scores high on authority, and here is the sentence that earned it. That is the difference between a defensible output and a black box. To be clear, this is the shape I am designing toward. Nothing has produced it yet.

shot.new_visual_element: the planned scored output, each score carrying its quoted evidence
shot.visual_intent: the deliverable made concrete and READABLE while the voice reacts to it. The file tab and the closing comment both mark it a DESIGN TARGET - nothing produced this, because nothing is built

the closing comment types in: NOT OUTPUT - this is the shape being designed

props.title: planned scored output — design target, not produced

beats.narration_text: So, back to the keyword question. The answer is no, and evaluation is how I prove it. I take a small set of brands labeled by hand, run the detector, and compare. If it only agrees when the obvious words are present, it is reading keywords. If it agrees on the brand that never says luxury, it is reading voice.

shot.new_visual_element: the hand-labelled set splitting keyword-reading from voice-reading
shot.visual_intent: WORKED EXAMPLE and Plain move 5 - pays off B02's prediction and states BOTH directions: agreement only on obvious words means keywords, agreement on the hard case means voice. Captioned illustrative, since no evaluation has been run

show.event: the evaluation question splits into two branches
left branch fills: it agrees only where the obvious words appear - that is keyword reading
right branch fills: it agrees on the brand that never says luxury - that is voice reading
both branches converge on a terracotta resolver: the hand-labelled set is what tells them apart
resolver holds - this is the test, not a result

beats.narration_text: Which brings me to what I actually need. The design is ready to be built against, but it cannot be tested without sample data. Three open questions: what format the samples arrive in, roughly how many brands we need, and who is gathering them. That is the thing blocking me this week.

shot.new_visual_element: the three open questions on sample data
shot.visual_intent: the ask made explicit and answerable. A progress update that names its blocker as three concrete questions is actionable; 'we need data' would not be

show.event: chip one lands: what format do the samples arrive in
chip two: roughly how many brands do we need
chip three: who is gathering them
chip four lands plainly: evaluation cannot start without this
caption settles - the design is not what is blocking the build

props.caption: the blocker is sample data — not the design, and not the build

beats.narration_text: The next step is not code either. The design goes through review and comes out as a proper software design document, and that is what gets built against. Then Ruler gets proven end to end, and only then does it make sense to scale to the other eleven archetypes. One rung at a time.

shot.new_visual_element: the route from design to scale, one rung done
shot.visual_intent: the plan shown as an ordered ladder so the viewer sees how little is finished. Only the first rung is accented, because only the first rung is done

rung two stacks beneath in plain ink: design review, producing a proper SDD
rung three: build and prove Ruler end to end
rung four: only then, scale to the other eleven
caption settles - one rung done, three to go

beats.narration_text: So, plainly, where this stands. Ruler is scoped. The design is drafted across inputs, scoring and evaluation. Nothing is built. There is no sample data yet, so there are no results, and the scored output I showed you was a design target, not a finding.

shot.new_visual_element: the five-chip status board, including what is NOT done
shot.visual_intent: the honesty beat. Three of the five chips are negative on purpose, so the board cannot be read as a progress brag. It is also the falsifiability beat: it names what would have to exist before any claim could be made

props.caption: design stage — the scored output shown earlier was a design target, not a finding

beats.narration_text: The sentence worth repeating: a score nobody can audit is not evidence. That is why every part of this design carries the copy behind it, and why evaluation comes before scale. Design drafted. Not built. Waiting on sample data. That is the honest state of week two.

shot.new_visual_element: artifact page holding the compressible sentence and the status
shot.visual_intent: Plain move 6 - one sentence that stays true if it is the only thing repeated secondhand, compressing the DISTINCTION rather than the topic. The status line sits on the page so the summary cannot be quoted as capability. Four numbered lines, no empty spacer

the one-line claim lands first and largest: a score nobody can audit is not evidence
the four lines list under it, in order
the last line holds alone: design drafted, not built, waiting on sample data

props.artifactHeading: A score nobody can audit is not evidence.
artifactLines: Inputs: what the brand actually publishes — never self-reported adjectives.
Scoring: every trait score carries the line of copy that earned it.
Evaluation: hand-labelled brands first, to prove it reads voice and not keywords.
Status: design drafted. Not built. Waiting on sample data.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: pick a brand you think has a strong personality, quote five lines of its actual published copy, and score it against one archetype, giving the exact line of evidence behind every score. Then check three things. Does every score cite a real quote. Could someone disagree with a score and point at the reason. And did it score the brand on voice, not on the obvious keywords.

shot.new_visual_element: the composer with the viewer's prompt and the three-point rubric beside it
shot.visual_intent: HANDOFF LAW plus nopunt SCAFFOLDED TASK - the prompt is read aloud verbatim then discussed, and the rubric is the same auditability standard the design itself is built on, so the viewer tests the idea rather than admiring it

running indicator reads 'paste this into Claude...'

rubric item 3 lands: voice, or just the obvious keywords

props.command: Pick a brand with a strong personality. Quote five lines of its actual published copy, then score it against one archetype — giving the exact line of evidence behind every single score.
output: Check the answer against three things:
1. does every score cite a real quote from the copy?
2. could someone disagree with a score and point at the reason?
3. did it score the brand's VOICE, or just the obvious keywords?

beats.narration_text: That's week two on Madison. More soon.
